name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

permissions:
  contents: read

# Cancel in-progress runs for the same branch/PR to avoid wasting CI minutes.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 'lts/*'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: 'npm ci --ignore-scripts'

      - name: Check generated nodes are up to date
        run: |
          npm run generate
          test -z "$(git status --porcelain -- nodes credentials package.json)"

      - name: Run lint
        run: 'npm run lint'

      - name: Run build
        run: 'npm run build'

      - name: Run tests
        run: 'npm test'

# OpenAPI spec gaps

Gaps in `https://mockingbird.n8n.io/openapi.json` that affect the generated nodes. Close them in the Mockingbird API repo, copy the new spec into this repo's `spec/openapi.json`, then run `npm run generate`.

Found 2026-10-10 against spec version 1.0.0.

## 1. No enums anywhere

The spec has no `enum` on any parameter or body field. Fields with a fixed set of values are plain strings. Generated nodes cannot build dropdowns from the spec. Today `scripts/generate.cjs` hard-codes an `ENUMS` table for the nodes that have known values, so users get dropdowns, but the lists can drift from the API.

Values below were read from live seed data. They show what exists today. They are not confirmed lists. Confirm them against the API code before adding the enums. Rare values may be missing.

| Endpoint | Field | Observed values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /tickets`, `POST /tickets`, `PATCH /tickets/{id}`, `PUT /tickets/{id}` | `status` | closed, open, pending, resolved |
| same | `priority` | high, low, normal, urgent |
| same | `category` | billing, defect, installation, other, shipping |
| `GET /orders`, `GET /orders/cursor` | `status` | cancelled, delivered, paid, pending, refunded, shipped |
| `GET /employees`, `POST /employees`, `PATCH /employees/{id}` | `status` | active, on_leave |
| same | `department` | engineering, finance, hr, ops, sales, support |
| `GET /time-off/requests`, `PATCH /time-off/requests/{id}` | `status` | approved, rejected (the PATCH summary also names a cancel action) |
| `GET /reviews` | `status` | published (moderation adds more) |
| `GET /reviews` | `rating` | 1 to 5 |
| `GET /customers` | `segment` | enterprise, mid_market, small |
| `GET /customers` | `country` | AT, AU, BR, CA, CH, DE, ES, FR, GB, IE, IN, IT, JP, NL, NO, PL, SE, SG, US |
| `GET /products` | `category` | bearings, compressors, controls, pumps, spares, valves |
| `GET /rates`, `GET /rates/convert` | `base`, `from`, `to` | EUR, USD, GBP, CHF, SEK, NOK, PLN, CZK, JPY, AUD (from the 422 message) |
| `GET /util/convert` | `from`, `to` | Units of one kind: length, mass, volume, temperature (c, f, k), or data (b, kb, mb, gb, tb). The exact unit names are not listed anywhere |
| `GET /fun/dogs/breed/{breed}/random` | `breed` | The keys returned by `GET /fun/dogs/breeds`. An unknown breed returns 404 |
| `GET /fun/trivia` | `category`, `difficulty` | Not found. An unknown difficulty returns an empty result, not an error |
| `GET /products`, `GET /products/{id}`, `GET /orders` | `fmt` | json, xml, csv, html (from the 406 message) |

Ask: add `enum` (or a shared enum schema) to each field. For `category` on products, link it to `GET /products/categories`.

## 2. Empty `fmt` returns 406

`GET /products?fmt=` returns `406 Unsupported format` with "'.' is not a supported extension". An empty value should be treated as not set. Clients that send every parameter, such as n8n, hit this.

## 3. Two response shapes depending on `paginate`

`paginate` on (default) returns `{ "data": [...], "meta": {...} }`. `paginate=false` returns a bare array of the whole set and ignores `page` and `limit`. The spec describes only the envelope. Ask: document both responses with `oneOf`, or add a separate path for the full set.

## 4. Generated operation IDs are unreadable

FastAPI default IDs such as `get_ticket_v1_tickets__ticket_id__get` are used. Generators cannot make good names from them. Ask: set an explicit `operation_id` on each route, for example `tickets_get`.

## 5. Request bodies that are not JSON

`POST /files` (multipart), and `POST /oauth/authorize` and `POST /oauth/token` (form-encoded), cannot be generated. The nodes skip them. Binary responses (PDF, zip, SVG, PNG, octet-stream) are skipped too.

## 6. Python clients get 403

A plain Python `urllib` request got `403 Forbidden` with a valid key, while curl worked. This is probably a user agent rule at the edge. Check whether it is intended.

## 7. `Idempotency-Key` is required but marked optional

`POST /reservations` returns 422 `missing-idempotency-key` without the header. The spec lists the header as optional. Mark it required.

## 8. Some ID minimums are not obvious

Reservation, booking, and fraud case IDs start at 100000. The spec has `minimum: 100000`, but the descriptions and examples do not say so. Id 1 returns 422.

## 9. List endpoints do not agree on pagination

`GET /employees` always returns a bare array, even with `paginate=true`, and honors `limit`. `GET /reviews`, `GET /time-off/requests`, and the other lists return `{ data, meta }`. `GET /reviews?paginate=false` returns all 3000 rows.

## 10. Moderation status shares a name with the list filter

`PATCH /reviews/{id}/moderate` takes `status` of `flagged` or `removed`. `GET /reviews` filters `status` by other values (`published`). The generator has one enum per field name, so Product Reviews gets no `status` dropdown.

## 11. More observed enums

| Endpoint | Field | Values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /jobs` | `type` | export_orders, report_sales, bulk_price_update |
| `POST /webhooks/fire`, `POST /webhooks/subscriptions` | `event_type`, `event_types` | order.created, ticket.updated, review.created, transaction.flagged |
| `POST /time-off/requests` | `leave_type` | annual, sick, unpaid, parental |
| `PATCH /time-off/requests/{id}` | `status` | pending, approved, rejected, cancelled |
| `PATCH /fraud/cases/{id}` | `status` | confirmed_fraud, cleared |
| `POST /agent/tickets/{id}/resolve` | `resolution_category` | resolved-info, replacement-shipped, refund-issued, no-fault-found, escalated |

# Publishes this n8n community node package to npm on every version tag push.
#
# Starting May 1 2026, n8n requires all community nodes to be published via
# GitHub Actions with npm provenance statements. This workflow satisfies that
# requirement. Provenance lets anyone cryptographically verify that a package
# was built by this exact workflow, from this exact repository and commit.
#
# ─── AUTHENTICATION ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC). No npm token exists in this repository.
# The trusted publisher on npmjs.com is set to:
#   Repository owner: n8n-io
#   Repository name:  n8n-nodes-mockingbird
#   Workflow name:    publish.yml
#   Environment:      (blank)
#   Allowed actions:  npm publish
# This configuration must exist on npmjs.com before a tag is pushed. The workflow
# filename must stay `publish.yml`, and the repository must stay `n8n-io/n8n-nodes-mockingbird`.
# Otherwise the OIDC exchange fails and the publish stops with an auth error.
#
# Two jobs keep dev dependency code away from the publish credential. The
# "verify" job runs lint, build, and tests and packs the tarball. It has no
# `id-token: write`. The "publish" job has it, installs nothing, runs no package
# code, and only publishes that tarball.
# This workflow publishes with `npm publish --provenance --access public`.
# Both OIDC and provenance need a public source repository and `id-token: write`.
# @n8n/node-cli is used only for lint and build.
#
# ─── TAG CONVENTION ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# This workflow triggers on tags matching "*.*.*" (e.g. 0.2.0).
# The tag must equal the version in package.json exactly. A "v" prefix
# (e.g. v0.2.0) fails the version check. If you want a prefix, change both the
# tag filter and the "Check the tag matches the package version" step.
# A version with a hyphen (e.g. 1.0.0-rc.1) is published under the "next" dist-tag.
#
# ─── RELEASE PROCESS ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# main is protected, so the version bump goes through a pull request:
#   1. Bump "version" in package.json and package-lock.json, and add a new
#      version heading to CHANGELOG.md.
#   2. Merge the pull request.
#   3. Tag the merge commit with the version (for example 0.2.0) and push the tag.
#   4. This workflow lints, builds, and publishes to npm with provenance.
#   5. Create the GitHub Release with the changelog notes.
#
# The workflow does not run `npm run release`. That command bumps, tags, and
# pushes to main from a developer machine, and it rewrites CHANGELOG.md.

name: Publish

on:
  push:
    tags:
      # Matches 0.1.0, 1.2.3, 2.0.0-rc.1, etc.
      # See "TAG CONVENTION" above. The tag must equal the package.json version.
      - '[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*'

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify and pack
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    # No id-token permission here, so lint, build, and test code cannot mint a publish credential.
    permissions:
      contents: read

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 'lts/*'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: 'npm ci --ignore-scripts'

      - name: Check the tag matches the package version
        run: |
          VERSION="$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")"
          if [ "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" != "$VERSION" ]; then
            echo "Tag $GITHUB_REF_NAME does not match package.json version $VERSION"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Lint, build, and test
        run: |
          npm run lint
          npm test

      - name: Pack
        # --ignore-scripts skips prepublishOnly and prepack.
        run: |
          mkdir pack
          npm pack --ignore-scripts --pack-destination pack

      - name: Upload the tarball
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: package
          path: pack/*.tgz
          if-no-files-found: error

  publish:
    name: Publish to npm
    needs: verify
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    permissions:
      # Mints the OIDC token. npm uses it to authenticate the publish
      # (Trusted Publishing) and to sign the provenance attestation.
      id-token: write
      contents: read

    steps:
      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 'lts/*'

      - name: Check npm supports Trusted Publishing
        # Trusted Publishing needs npm 11.5.1 or later and there is no token fallback.
        run: |
          npm --version
          node -e "const [a,b,c]=process.argv[1].split('.').map(n=>parseInt(n,10));process.exit(a>11||(a===11&&(b>5||(b===5&&c>=1)))?0:1)" "$(npm --version)" || { echo 'npm 11.5.1 or later is required'; exit 1; }

      - name: Download the tarball
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: package
          path: pack

      - name: Publish
        # Authenticates with the GitHub OIDC token (npm Trusted Publishing).
        # The tarball comes from the verify job. No package code runs here.
        run: |
          # The ./ prefix stops npm from reading the path as a GitHub owner/repo shorthand.
          TARBALL="./$(ls pack/*.tgz)"
          VERSION="$(tar -xOzf "$TARBALL" package/package.json | node -p "JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync(0,'utf8')).version")"
          if [ "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" != "$VERSION" ]; then
            echo "Tag $GITHUB_REF_NAME does not match tarball version $VERSION"
            exit 1
          fi
          DIST_TAG=latest
          case "$VERSION" in *-*) DIST_TAG=next ;; esac
          npm publish "$TARBALL" --provenance --access public --tag "$DIST_TAG"

# n8n-nodes-mockingbird

n8n community nodes for [Mockingbird](https://mockingbird.n8n.io), the stable mock APIs used in n8n courses, demos, and content.

[n8n](https://n8n.io/) is the platform for AI agents and workflows: the one place to build, run, and manage them, from a first prototype to enterprise scale.

[Installation](#installation)
[Nodes](#nodes)
[Credentials](#credentials)
[Usage](#usage)
[Development](#development)

## Installation

Follow the [installation guide](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/community-nodes/installation/) in the n8n community nodes documentation.

## Nodes

Six nodes group the Mockingbird APIs by theme. Pick the node, then a resource, then an operation.

| Node                             | Resources                                      | Credential |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ---------- |
| Mockingbird Commerce             | Product, Order, Inventory, Review, Customer    | Optional   |
| Mockingbird Support              | Ticket, Article, Agent Tool, Text              | Required   |
| Mockingbird People               | Employee, Time Off Request, Room               | Required   |
| Mockingbird Finance and Security | Transaction, Security, Exchange Rate           | Optional   |
| Mockingbird Platform             | Job, Event, Webhook, File, Sandbox, Assessment | Optional   |
| Mockingbird Fun and Utilities    | Fun, Utility, Weather, Quote                   | Optional   |

Some resources need no credential. Examples are Product, Weather, and Exchange Rate. In a node marked Optional, a resource that needs a key fails with 401 if you add no credential. Nodes marked Required always need one.

### Operations

| Resource         | Operations                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Product          | Get, Get Many, Get Categories                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Order            | Get, Get Many, Get Many (Cursor)                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Inventory        | Get, Create Reservation, Delete Reservation                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Review           | Get Many, Get Latest, Create, Moderate                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Customer         | Get, Get Many, Create                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Ticket           | Get, Get Many, Create, Update, Replace, Add Comment                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Article          | Search, Get                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Agent Tool       | Look Up Customer, Refund Order, Cancel Order, Resend Invoice, Get Next Ticket, Resolve Ticket, Get Tools                                                                                                               |
| Text             | Classify Sentiment, Classify Intent, Extract Entities                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Employee         | Get, Get Many, Create, Update, Get Reports, Get Departments, Get Org Chart, Get Salary Bands                                                                                                                           |
| Time Off Request | Get Many, Get Many by Employee, Create, Update, Get Balance, Get Calendar                                                                                                                                              |
| Room             | Get Many, Get Availability, Create Booking, Delete Booking                                                                                                                                                             |
| Transaction      | Get, Get Many, Score, Create Case, Update Case                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Security         | Get Many Events, Get Many Blocks, Create Block                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Exchange Rate    | Get Rates, Convert                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Job              | Create, Get, Get Result                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Event            | Get Many                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Webhook          | Get Many Subscriptions, Create Subscription, Delete Subscription, Fire                                                                                                                                                 |
| File             | Get Many                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Sandbox          | Reset, Get ID                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Assessment       | Get, Get Many, Get Source, Submit                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Fun              | Get Random Dog, Get Dog Breeds, Get Random Dog by Breed, Get Random Cat, Get Random Robot, Get Random Joke, Get Joke, Get Random Fact, Get Random Activity, Get Trivia, Get Random Users, Get Number Fact, Get Fortune |
| Utility          | Get Countries, Echo, Respond With Status, Respond After Delay, Generate UUID, Hash Text, Encode Base64, Decode Base64, Validate Email, Validate IBAN, Validate VAT Number, Convert Units, Generate Lorem Ipsum         |
| Weather          | Get Current, Get Forecast                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Quote            | Get, Get Many, Get Quote of the Day                                                                                                                                                                                    |

**Get Many (Cursor)** makes one request and returns the full `{ data, meta }` response. It does not follow `meta.next_cursor`. Pass the cursor back in Additional Fields to read the next page.

## Credentials

Some resources need no credential, such as Product and Weather. See the Nodes table.

1. Get an API key from the Mockingbird dashboard.
2. Create a **Mockingbird API** credential in n8n.
3. Enter the API key.
4. Choose the ID type: **Sandbox** (default) or **Assessment**.
5. Enter the ID.

### About the ID

The ID is only for temporary writes and per-learner state. Reads of seed data ignore it.

- **Sandbox** is for everyone. It is sent as `X-Sandbox-Id`. To get a new ID, call `GET /v1/sandbox-id`.
- **Assessment** is for Academy learners. It is sent as `X-Assessment-Id`. Use the ID your course gave you.
- Format: 8 to 64 characters from `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -`.
- Rows you create are stored under the ID for 48 hours. Two callers with the same ID share rows.
- Assessments use the ID to pick your row set and to credit your pass.
- Idempotency keys are scoped by the ID.

Send only one of the two headers. The credential does this for you.

The credential also works with the HTTP Request node as a predefined credential type.

## Usage

Add a Mockingbird node to a workflow. Pick a resource and an operation. Example: Mockingbird Commerce, Product, Get Many, with `Search` set to `chair`.

## Development

Nodes are generated from `spec/openapi.json` with `@devlikeapro/n8n-openapi-node`. Edit `scripts/generate.cjs`, not the files in `generated/`.

```bash
npm run generate
npm run build
npm run lint
```

CI fails when generated files drift from the spec.

# n8n community node

## Overview
This is a project containing code for an n8n community node. n8n is a workflow
automation platform where users build workflows with nodes, which are the
building block of a workflow. Nodes can perform a range of actions, such as
starting a workflow (called a "trigger node"), fetching and sending data, or
processing and manipulating it. Besides that there are credentials - entities
that store sensitive information on how to connect to external services and
APIs. A node can require some credentials to be used. Community nodes are a way
for anyone to create such nodes and add them to be used in n8n. All community
nodes are named in a format: `n8n-nodes-<n>` or `@org/n8n-nodes-<n>`.
Community nodes can also be submitted for approval to be used on n8n Cloud
version. In that case there are rules that the node needs to follow in order to
be approved

## Important notes
- Follow the **rules and guidelines in this document and the linked docs
  below** over any code examples.
- All code blocks in these docs are **illustrative and incomplete**.
  They **MUST NOT** be copied verbatim or assumed to be the final desired code.
- Replace example names like `Example`, `Wordpress`, `wordpressApi`, etc.
  with names that match the **actual service / node** you are building.
- When in doubt, **generalize from the patterns**, don't replicate the exact
  structure, fields, or values from the examples.
- Produce the **full implementation** needed for the current project
  (nodes, credentials, tests, etc.), not just fragments similar to examples.
- If an example omits parts (e.g. types, operations, properties), **infer and
  implement the missing parts** based on the real requirements / API docs.
- Never output `Wordpress`-specific code unless the project is actually about
  WordPress.

## Project structure
There are two main folders in this project:
- `nodes` contains all of the nodes in a package (there can be more than 1).
  The code for each node usually lives in its own folder
- `credentials` contains all of the credentials in a package. Usually it's just
  a single file for every credential
So it looks something like this:
.
├── nodes/
│   └── Example/
│       ├── Example.node.ts
│       └── ...
├── credentials/
│   └── Example.credentials.ts
├── package.json
└── ...
It's important to note that `package.json` has a special field `n8n` that have
information about nodes and credentials in a package:
```json
{
  "name": "n8n-nodes-example",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "n8n": {
    "n8nNodesApiVersion": 1,
    "strict": true,
    "credentials": [
        "dist/credentials/Example.credentials.js"
    ],
    "nodes": [
      "dist/nodes/Example/Example.node.js"
    ]
  }
}
```
`nodes` and `credentials` keys contain paths to transpiled JS files in a `dist`
folder for the nodes and credentials respectively. If you add/remove/rename
nodes and/or credentials, you need to make sure to update `n8n.nodes` and
`n8n.credentials` keys in `package.json` accordingly. Initial files in the
project _may_ contain example nodes and/or credentials that need to be
**removed or renamed** once you start making an actual node.

## Key guidelines
- Use the `n8n-node` CLI tool **whenever possible** for building, dev mode,
  linting, etc.
- **Always** address any lint/typecheck errors/warnings, unless there is a
  **very specific reason** to ignore/disable it
- Make sure to use **proper types whenever possible**
- If you are updating the npm package version, make sure to **update
  CHANGELOG.md** in the root of the repository
- Read `.agents/workflow.md` for more info

## Context-specific docs
Load these before working on the relevant area:

| Working on...                        | Read first                                                          |
|--------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Any node file in `nodes/`            | `.agents/nodes.md` and `.agents/properties.md`                      |
| A declarative-style node             | above + `.agents/nodes-declarative.md`                              |
| A programmatic-style node            | above + `.agents/nodes-programmatic.md`                             |
| Files in `credentials/`              | `.agents/credentials.md`                                            |
| Adding a new version to a node       | `.agents/versioning.md`                                             |
| Starting a new task or planning      | `.agents/workflow.md`                                               |

regarding building community nodes:

- https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/creating-nodes/overview/
